verses.text: Woe to the bloodstained city! It is packed with lies and plunder; the looting never stops.
Listen to the crack of whips, the clatter of wheels, the pounding horses, and the bouncing chariots!
Cavalry charges; swords flash and spears glitter. The dead pile up, and bodies are everywhere. People stumble over the corpses.
This happened because of the countless acts of the alluring prostitute, mistress of sorcery, who sold nations through her prostitution and families through her spells.
“Look, I am against you,” says the LORD of Armies. “I will pull up your skirt over your face and show the nations your nakedness, the kingdoms your shame.
“I will cover you with filth, treat you with contempt, and make you a public spectacle.
“Everyone who sees you will run away and say, ‘Nineveh is destroyed! Who will mourn for her?’ Where can I find anyone to comfort you?”
“Are you better than No-Amon, surrounded by rivers and protected by waters—its rampart the sea, its wall the sea?
Cush and Egypt gave it limitless strength. Put and Libya supported it.
“Yet it too was carried off into exile. Its young children were smashed at every street corner. Soldiers cast lots for its nobles, and all its important people were chained up.
“You too will become drunk and hide. You too will search for a refuge from the enemy.
“All your fortresses are like fig trees with ripe first figs. Shake them, and they fall straight into the eater’s mouth.
“Look, your troops have become like women. The gates of your land stand wide open to your enemies; fire has burned up the bars.
“Draw water for the siege. Strengthen your fortresses. Get into the mud and stomp it; strengthen the brick kiln.
“But fire will consume you there, and the sword will cut you down. It will devour you like locusts. Multiply like grasshoppers; multiply like locusts!
“You made your merchants more numerous than the stars in the sky. Like locusts, they strip the land and then fly away.
“Your guards are like locusts, and your officials like swarms of grasshoppers. They settle on the walls on a cold day, but when the sun comes out, they fly away; no one knows where they went.
“Your shepherds are asleep, king of Assyria; your nobles lie down. Your people are scattered across the mountains, with no one to gather them.
“There is no healing your wound; your injury is fatal. Everyone who hears the news about you claps their hands. Who hasn’t suffered from your endless cruelty?”
